summary:
MissionX – Space Mission Designer is an interactive browser-based educational game developed to demonstrate the challenges of designing a space mission. Players take the role of mission planners and design their own spacecraft by selecting a destination (Moon or Mars), launch vehicle, power system, scientific instruments and communication equipment.

The game focuses on resource management by calculating the spacecraft's total budget, mass and power requirements. Players can run a mission simulation to evaluate whether their spacecraft design meets the available resource limits and receive a mission success or failure report.

MissionX addresses the Space Mission Design Game challenge by making space mission planning interactive and accessible. It helps students understand engineering trade-offs, resource limitations and the importance of making suitable decisions when planning space exploration missions. The project aims to make learning about space technology more engaging through game-based simulation.
details:
Project Details – MissionX: Space Mission Designer

MissionX is an interactive, browser-based educational game that introduces users to the basic concepts of spacecraft design and space mission planning. It allows players to take the role of mission planners and create a spacecraft for a journey to either the Moon or Mars.

How It Works

Users begin by selecting a destination: the Moon or Mars. They then customize their spacecraft by choosing a launch vehicle, power system, scientific instruments, and communication equipment. Based on these selections, the game calculates the estimated spacecraft mass, budget, and power requirements. Players can run a mission simulation to check whether their spacecraft design meets the available resource limits. The simulation then provides a mission success or failure report.

Benefits and Intended Impact

MissionX makes the basic ideas behind space mission planning easier and more engaging to understand. It helps students explore resource management, engineering trade-offs, and decision-making. By allowing users to experiment with different spacecraft configurations, the project encourages curiosity about space exploration, science, and engineering.

Tools and Technologies

The project was developed as a browser-based application using:

  • HTML – for the structure of the application.
  • CSS – for the user interface and visual design.
  • JavaScript – for spacecraft selection, resource calculations, and simulation logic.
  • Web browser – to run the application without requiring additional software installation.

Creativity and Design Considerations

The creative aspect of MissionX is its game-based approach to learning about spacecraft design. Instead of only reading about space missions, users can make their own design choices and immediately see how those choices affect mission resources and outcomes.

During development, we considered simplicity, ease of use, interactive learning, and the importance of balancing spacecraft mass, power, and budget. The project uses a simplified educational simulation to demonstrate the basic challenges involved in planning a space mission.
